title: Pyrazolyl–triazolyl chalcones as promising antimycobacterial candidates: integrating experimental and computational insights
content: In pursuit of developing novel antitubercular scaffolds, a series of pyrazolyl–triazolyl-functionalized chalcones (6a–o) were synthesized and evaluated for their antimycobacterial activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv using the MABA assay. The synthesized compounds exhibited promising inhibitory potential, with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values ranging from 1.6 to 12.5 µg mL−1. Among them, compounds 6b and 6k emerged as the most potent analogues (MIC = 1.6 µg mL−1), followed by compounds 6c, 6d, 6g, 6h, 6j, and 6l displaying strong activity (MIC = 3.12 µg mL−1). Molecular docking studies against M. tuberculosis enoyl-ACP reductase (InhA; PDB ID: 4TZK) demonstrated strong binding affinities (−7.8 to −8.5 kcal mol−1), with the potent compounds forming dense networks of π-anion interactions with NAD, π–π stacking interactions with PHE97/TYR158, and π-sulfur interactions with MET161/MET199. ADME profiling further confirmed the favorable pharmacokinetic behavior of most derivatives, except that of 6n. These combined biological, computational, and physicochemical findings position the synthesized chalcone–pyrazole–triazole hybrids as promising lead candidates for further antitubercular drug development.
